text: 2027 Global Energy Exhibition and Conference set to open in Hanoi

The Global Energy Exhibition and Conference Vietnam 2027 (GEEC 2027) is scheduled to take place in Hanoi from May 26-28, 2027, under the theme "Where Asia's Energy Future Takes Shape", according to the organizing board.
The event is expected to highlight Vietnam's growing role in international energy security as the country faces substantial investment requirements for power generation and infrastructure.

Addressing a press conference held in Hanoi on November 17 to announce the event, Deputy Minister of Industry and Trade Truong Thanh Hoai said achieving key objectives, including diversifying energy supplies, developing power generation and transmission infrastructure, advancing technology and improving energy efficiency, would require additional financial, technological and management resources, particularly from international partners and the private sector.
He described GEEC 2027 as a practical platform for addressing these needs.

The Ministry of Industry and Trade expects the event to facilitate policy discussions and information exchange among international partners, businesses and energy experts, while creating opportunities for partnerships, technology development, workforce improvement and greater participation by Vietnamese companies in global supply chains.
The exhibition is expected to cover six halls, accommodating more than 800 exhibitors, 450 speakers and 120 conference sessions, and attracting approximately 30,000 visitors.

Four specialised sections will showcase power generation and grid infrastructure; LNG, gas and energy security; renewable energy and storage; and green transport, electric vehicle infrastructure, electrification, AI and digitalisation.
National pavilions, innovation showcases and dedicated spaces for young people and the Global Energy Club will also feature.
National pavilions from Italy, China, Germany and the UAE are expected to participate, alongside major Vietnamese groups such as PVN and EVN.

A series of strategic conferences, technical sessions, high-level roundtables and business matchmaking programmes will run alongside the exhibition, with the event expected to generate new foreign direct investment (FDI) and business cooperation opportunities.
